articles.title: JPMorgan Chase unveils new 60-story headquarters, reshaping New York City's skyline
articles.content: JPMorgan Chase unveiled its new 60-story headquarters to the public on Monday, one of the first major office buildings to be constructed after the COVID-19 pandemic and one that will remake the New York City skyline for decades. The bronze and steel tower at 270 Park, which reportedly cost $3 billion, replaced the Union Carbide Building, which sat on a full city block at 48th Street and Park Avenue for nearly 60 years. JPMorgan expects to house roughly 10,000 of its 24,000 New York-based employees in the new building, with employees starting their first workday at the tower at the same time as the company holds its ribbon cutting ceremony.

articles.title: Jamie Dimon Sees Risks in the Stock Market. It Isn’t the First Time.
articles.content: Former British Prime Minister Winston Churchill was quoted more than a century ago as saying that his greatest political challenge was that of “events,” or the unknown circumstances that can ultimately bring down a government. JPMorgan Chase boss Jamie Dimon, the son of a stockbroker and as steeped in financial market knowledge as any executive on Wall Street, has seen more than a few of his forecasts fall flat recently. The culprit has generally been what the late Donald Rumsfeld famously described as “unknown unknowns”.
